neighbours.label: A connective that introduces a justification or explanation of the preceding clause (', because', ', for', 'Disclaimer:')
fire: The farmers were worried all spring, because the river had already flooded twice that year.
We decided to stay home that evening, because the roads were covered in ice.
The soldiers should have waited, for the town was far too well defended to take quickly.
The bakery closed early on Friday, because the oven had broken down at noon.
It is a strange name for a flower, because the plant actually grows in dry sand.
Her parents finally accepted the boyfriend, because it was clear he was here to stay.
The trail was closed to hikers, because a bear had been seen near the campsite.
Nobody touched the cake at the party, for everyone knew it was meant for the bride.
quiet: The farmers were worried all spring, and the river flooded twice that year.
We decided to stay home that evening and watched a film by the fire.
The soldiers waited outside the town for three days before the gates opened.
The bakery closed early on Friday, and the staff went home at noon.
It is a strange name for a flower that grows in the dry sand of the dunes.
Her parents finally accepted the boyfriend, and he came to dinner on Sunday.
The trail was closed to hikers, and the rangers put up a sign near the campsite.
Nobody touched the cake at the party until the bride arrived with her family.

notes: Card: top 32 peak on ':' x12 (often 'Disclaimer:'), ' for' x7, ' because' x5, ' denn', ' Or'; the shared pattern is a connective that opens a justification. Near misses use ' and' in the same slot.
